article.headline: HiChord Is the Pocket Synth That Knows Every Chord
article.lede: A Toronto company called Pocket Audio has built a device the size of a deck of cards that can play 882 chords, loop audio, and drive a full drum machine — no music theory required. The HiChord 1.0 shipped to Kickstarter backers in early 2026. @mrblackstudio wants one.
article.body:
The HiChord is, at its core, a *chord synthesizer*: a gadget that stores harmonic combinations and plays them on demand, sparing the user from having to know that a D-minor seventh requires fingers on four specific frets. Pocket Audio has loaded 882 chords across 28 chord types into hardware roughly 100 mm × 71 mm — smaller than most phones.

The engineering inside is more serious than the toy-like pitch suggests. The device runs on an Electrosmith **Daisy** DSP platform, a microcontroller popular with boutique instrument builders, and offers four synthesis engines including *FM synthesis* (frequency modulation, the technique behind the metallic tones of 1980s digital keyboards). Twelve oscillators run simultaneously. A built-in microphone lets users sample ambient sounds and map them across the chord grid.

It also functions as a *MIDI controller* — meaning it can send note and chord data over USB-C to professional software like Ableton Live or Logic Pro, folding into a serious production setup rather than sitting beside it. This dual life as standalone toy and studio peripheral explains much of the appeal among producers.

At $249 for the standard edition and $320 for aluminum, HiChord sits in the middle of the boutique hardware market — cheaper than a Teenage Engineering OP-1, pricier than a Teenage Engineering Pocket Operator. The Kickstarter model, with mid-February 2026 delivery, is the classic mechanism for validating demand before committing to mass production runs. Whether the device finds a durable audience beyond its early adopters will depend on whether the chord-grid concept genuinely lowers the barrier to music-making or simply flatters buyers into thinking they have.

concepts.definition: An instrument that generates multiple musical notes simultaneously to produce a harmony. Unlike a traditional keyboard where the player must know and finger each note, a chord synthesizer stores complete chord shapes and plays them with a single button press.

Frequency modulation synthesis is a method of generating sound by using one waveform (the modulator) to alter the frequency of another (the carrier). It produces the bright, metallic, or glassy timbres associated with 1980s digital keyboards like the Yamaha DX7.

A hardware device that sends performance data — note pitch, velocity, timing — to a computer or synthesizer using the MIDI protocol, rather than generating sound itself. It allows musicians to play software instruments inside a DAW using physical buttons, keys, or pads.

A microcontroller platform from Electrosmith designed specifically for audio applications. Popular in the boutique instrument-building community, it handles digital signal processing tasks — synthesis, effects, sampling — and is frequently found inside independent hardware music devices.
A colloquial term among musicians and producers for the compulsive desire to buy new instruments or equipment. The tweet's 'I don't need it, but so want it' is a textbook GAS declaration.
